A 30-year-old woman had acute rheumatic fever as a child and when she was around 20 years of age she developed a new cardiac murmur. Now she presents with fever, intermittent severe pain in the left upper quadrant of her abdomen, and Roth spots in the retina. At the present time one culture submitted to the hospital laboratory grew out a specific type of bacteria. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her disease?

A 10-year-old boy has experienced increased fatigue and decreased exercise tolerance for the past 2 weeks. He presented with an acute onset of fever, and pain in several joints 2 weeks before. Physical examination finds an enlarged heart and systolic murmur. Laboratory tests find an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and an elevated antistreptolysin O titer. Which of the following lesions is most likely to be found in the heart of this patient?

options.A: Foci of fibrinoid necrosis surrounded with Anitsehkow cells in the interstitial tissue of the heart
options.B: Large fragile vegetations formed along the lines of closure of the mitral valves
options.C: Coagulative necrosis of the cardiac fibers with neutrophilic infiltration
options.D: Haphazardly arranged hypertrophied myocytes in the interventricular septum
options.E: Mural thrombosis in the left atrium

questions.title: A 30-year-old man who has a history of rheumatic fever during childhood presents with shortness of breath and cough. Physical examination finds an early diastolic opening snap with a rumbling late diastolic murmur. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man presents with signs of angina, syncopal episodes with exertion and left heart failure. Physical examination reveals a midsystolic ejection murmur. Pressure studies reveal that the left ventricular pressure during systole is markedly greater than the aortic pressure. Which of the following is the most frequent cause of the cardiac valvular abnormality present in this patient?

A 65-year-old man presents shortness of breath, cough, and nocturnal dyspnea. Physical examination reveals a hyperdynamic, bounding, "water-hammer" pulse and a diastolic murmur. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman presents with increasing chest pain and occasional syncopal episodes, especially with physical exertion. She has nocturnal dyspnea and orthopnea. Physical examination reveals a midsystolic ejection murmur. An echocardiogram shows concentric hypertrophy of the left ventricle. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman developed left heart failure and died suddenly. A section from her heart at the time of autopsy reveals marked thickening of the wall of the left ventricle with decrease in cavity size, but the thickness of the right ventricle is within normal limits. Many of the nuclei of the myocytes in the wall of the left ventricle are hyperchromatic and rectangular. The endocardium and the cardiac valves are normal. What is the most likely cause of this cardiac pathology?

Several days after a myocardial infarction, a 60-year-old man develops a sudden onset of a new pansystolic murmur along with a diastolic flow murmur. Workup reveals increased left atrial pressure that develops late in systole and extends into diastole. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the abnormalities present in this individual?

options.A: Thrombosis of the left atrial cavity
options.C: Rupture of the left ventricular wall
options.D: Aneurysmal dilation of the left ventricle

questions.title: Areas of myocardial infarction undergo a series of gross changes. Which of the following is the earliest histologic change in myocardial infarction?

options.C: Liquefaction necrosis of cardiac muscle fibers
options.D: Hyperemia and hemorrhage in the border zone around the infarction

questions.title: Which of the following complications will be eariest to arise following a transmural myocardial infarction?

A 65-year-old man develops intense crushing substernal, chest pain that is not relieved by nitroglycerin. The ECG shows ST-segment elevation and abnormal Q waves. His condition rapidly worsens and he dies 2 days later. At autopsy a 2.5 cm^2 necrotic area is found that involves the anterior left ventricle. What is the most likely cause of this patient's myocardial infarction?

options.A: Fibrinoid necrosis of main trunk of left coronary artery
options.B: Severe stenosis of all three main branches of coronary artery without thrombosis
options.C: Thrombosis of the anterior descending branch of the left coronary artery
options.D: Complete occlusion of the left circumflex coronary artery
options.E: Vasospasm of the right coronary artery

A 65-year-old man has a long history of poorly controlled hypertension. On physical examination, he is afebrile. His neck veins are distended. Crepitant rales can be heard in both lower lungs. He has pitting edema of his feet bilaterally and mild hepatomegaly. A chest x-ray reveals his heart is dilated and enlarged. options.C: Decreased peripheral resistance caused by low-output cardiac failure
options.D: Increased afterload caused by systolic dysfunction of the heart
options.E: Increased preload caused by diastolic dysfunction of his heart

A 33-year-old man presents with signs and symptoms of hyperglycemia. Laboratory evaluation of his serum also finds hypertriglyceridemia, which is due to his diabetes. The most common type of secondary hyperlipidemia associated with diabetes mellitus is characterized by elevated serum levels of which one of the following substances?

A 30-year-old woman has angina pectoris of 6 months duration. On physical examination, her blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg. She is 162 cm tall and weighs 80 kg. Coronary angiography shows 75% narrowing of the anterior descending branch of the left coronary artery. Which of the following is the major risk factor associated with these findings?

For more than a decade, a 40-year-old man has had poorly controlled hypertension ranging from 150/90 mmHg to 160/95 mmHg. Over the past 3 months, his blood pressure has increased to 250/125 mmHg. A chest radiograph shows a prominent border on the left side of the heart. Laboratory studies show that his serum creatinine level has increased during this time from 1.7 mg/dL to 3.8 mg/dL. Which of the following lesions is most likely to be found in the afferent glomerular arterioles of this patient?

A 60-year-old woman has reported increasing fatigue over the past year. Laboratory studies show a serum creatinine level of 4.7 mg/dL（normal values: male: 0.6-1.2 mg/dl, female: 0.5-1.1 mg/dl） and urea nitrogen level of 44 mg/dL (normal value: adult: 9-20 mg/dl, child: 5-18 mg/dl). An abdominal ultrasound scan shows that her kidneys are symmetrically shrunken and granular. The high-magnification microscopic appearance of the kidneys is shown. These findings are most likely to indicate which of the following underlying conditions?

options.D: Advanced breast carcinoma with widespread metastasis

options.B: Collection of foam cells, necrotic areas, cholesterol clefts and calcification

options.D: A core of lipid debris covered by a cap of smooth muscle cells
options.E: Lipid-filled foam cells and T lymphocytes

options.A: Increasing stenosis of right coronary artery
options.B: Hypertrophy of ischemic myocardium with increased oxygen demand

options.E: Fissuring of plaque in left coronary artery with superimposed mural (partial) thrombosis

Which of the following serum laboratory findings is most characteristic of the disease affecting this patient?

options.B: Positive blood culture for Staphylococcus aureus

questions.title: A 37-year-old woman dies suddenly at home. External examination of the body shows no evidence of trauma. The microscopic appearance of the proximal left anterior descending artery at autopsy is shown. Which of the following conditions is most likely to be the underlying cause of death?

options.E: Advanced breast carcinoma with widespread metastases

A 16-year-old girl has fever and chest pain. Two weeks earlier, she had a mild upper respiratory tract infection. On physical examination, her temperature is 37°C, pulse 90/min, respirations 20/min, and blood pressure 85/45 mmHg. A friction rub is audible on auscultation of the chest. Which of the following additional complications of this illness is most likely to be seen in the patient?
